image_description:
1. **Chart type**: Circular hierarchical **treemap / Voronoi treemap**.

2. **Layout techniques**:
- **Hierarchical nesting**: Large regions contain smaller subregions.
- **Partitioned by category**: The circle is split into two top-level groups.
- **Area encoding**: Region size represents amount.
- **Color grouping**: Two colors distinguish the two top-level plans.
- No axes, no faceting, no stacking.

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Plan (Infrastructure plan, Families plan) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue; top-level grouped region within the circle; legend |
| Major spending category (e.g., Transportation, Buildings and Utilities, In-Home Care, Jobs and Innovation, Tax Credits, Child and Family Support, Education, I.R.S.) | Categorical/nominal | Nested region/grouping; text label |
| Program / line item within category (e.g., Roads and bridges, Affordable housing, Child care, Pell grants, etc.) | Categorical/nominal | Individual polygon region; text label |
| Amount ($ billions / trillions) | Quantitative | Area/size of regions; numeric text labels inside regions; totals in legend |

Visible note:
- Units are stated as **amounts on the chart in billions**, while top-level legend totals are shown in **trillions**.

image_description:
1. **Chart type**: Circular hierarchical **treemap / Voronoi treemap**.

2. **Layout techniques**:
- **Hierarchical nesting**: Large regions contain smaller subregions.
- **Partitioned by category**: The circle is split into two top-level groups.
- **Area encoding**: Region size represents amount.
- **Color grouping**: Two colors distinguish the two top-level plans.
- No axes, no faceting, no stacking.

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Plan (Infrastructure plan, Families plan) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue; top-level grouped region within the circle; legend |
| Major spending category (e.g., Transportation, Buildings and Utilities, In-Home Care, Jobs and Innovation, Tax Credits, Child and Family Support, Education, I.R.S.) | Categorical/nominal | Nested region/grouping; text label |
| Program / line item within category (e.g., Roads and bridges, Affordable housing, Child care, Pell grants, etc.) | Categorical/nominal | Individual polygon region; text label |
| Amount ($ billions / trillions) | Quantitative | Area/size of regions; numeric text labels inside regions; totals in legend |

Visible note:
- Units are stated as **amounts on the chart in billions**, while top-level legend totals are shown in **trillions**.

image_description:
1. **Chart type**: Circular hierarchical **treemap / Voronoi treemap**.

2. **Layout techniques**:
- **Hierarchical nesting**: Large regions contain smaller subregions.
- **Partitioned by category**: The circle is split into two top-level groups.
- **Area encoding**: Region size represents amount.
- **Color grouping**: Two colors distinguish the two top-level plans.
- No axes, no faceting, no stacking.

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Plan (Infrastructure plan, Families plan) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue; top-level grouped region within the circle; legend |
| Major spending category (e.g., Transportation, Buildings and Utilities, In-Home Care, Jobs and Innovation, Tax Credits, Child and Family Support, Education, I.R.S.) | Categorical/nominal | Nested region/grouping; text label |
| Program / line item within category (e.g., Roads and bridges, Affordable housing, Child care, Pell grants, etc.) | Categorical/nominal | Individual polygon region; text label |
| Amount ($ billions / trillions) | Quantitative | Area/size of regions; numeric text labels inside regions; totals in legend |

Visible note:
- Units are stated as **amounts on the chart in billions**, while top-level legend totals are shown in **trillions**.

image_description:
1. **Chart type**: Circular hierarchical **treemap / Voronoi treemap**.

2. **Layout techniques**:
- **Hierarchical nesting**: Large regions contain smaller subregions.
- **Partitioned by category**: The circle is split into two top-level groups.
- **Area encoding**: Region size represents amount.
- **Color grouping**: Two colors distinguish the two top-level plans.
- No axes, no faceting, no stacking.

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Plan (Infrastructure plan, Families plan) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue; top-level grouped region within the circle; legend |
| Major spending category (e.g., Transportation, Buildings and Utilities, In-Home Care, Jobs and Innovation, Tax Credits, Child and Family Support, Education, I.R.S.) | Categorical/nominal | Nested region/grouping; text label |
| Program / line item within category (e.g., Roads and bridges, Affordable housing, Child care, Pell grants, etc.) | Categorical/nominal | Individual polygon region; text label |
| Amount ($ billions / trillions) | Quantitative | Area/size of regions; numeric text labels inside regions; totals in legend |

raw_comment:
“President Biden’s New Plan For The Future”

After analyzing the graph we noticed that The $4.1 trillion plan is split into two categories: infrastructure plan and families plan. Also, some of the categories are only split into two subcategories like tax credits, but other categories have many subcategories like jobs and innovation. The category with the most spending is in tax credits: expansion of child earned income and child dependent care tax credits. We also wonder why a small amount of money is being spent on teachers as they are very important to our society. We also wonder how the public will take President Biden’s plan and why the graph wasn’t split into a pie chart instead of two halves of a circle. This impacts our community because what the money is being spent on impacts everyone in different ways in our everyday lives. As students who are going into college, 2 years of free community college is a lot of saved money.

image_description:
1. **Chart type**: Circular hierarchical **treemap / Voronoi treemap**.

2. **Layout techniques**:
- **Hierarchical nesting**: Large regions contain smaller subregions.
- **Partitioned by category**: The circle is split into two top-level groups.
- **Area encoding**: Region size represents amount.
- **Color grouping**: Two colors distinguish the two top-level plans.
- No axes, no faceting, no stacking.

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Plan (Infrastructure plan, Families plan) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue; top-level grouped region within the circle; legend |
| Major spending category (e.g., Transportation, Buildings and Utilities, In-Home Care, Jobs and Innovation, Tax Credits, Child and Family Support, Education, I.R.S.) | Categorical/nominal | Nested region/grouping; text label |
| Program / line item within category (e.g., Roads and bridges, Affordable housing, Child care, Pell grants, etc.) | Categorical/nominal | Individual polygon region; text label |
| Amount ($ billions / trillions) | Quantitative | Area/size of regions; numeric text labels inside regions; totals in legend |

Visible note:
- Units are stated as **amounts on the chart in billions**, while top-level legend totals are shown in **trillions**.

raw_comment:
Welcome to Wednesday's moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  

Today’s graph shows the two parts of President Biden’s economic plan:  $2.3 trillion Infrastructure Plan and $1.8 trillion Families Plan.  The diagram shows the President’s allocation of the $4.1 trillion of new spending and tax cuts to 50 programs.   The infrastructure plan would involve 8 years of spending paid for with 15 years of higher corporate taxes.  The Families Plan would cover over 10 years of spending and taxes on the wealthiest Americans.   To add some  perspective on these very large numbers, the 2020 annual U.S. Gross Domestic Product, a measure of the size of the economy, was $21.4 trillion. The recently released 2020 U.S. Census found 331 million people. 

From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online.

By Friday morning, we’ll reveal the article that included this graphic and much more.  We look forward to reading your discoveries.

Note that you can get a link to your response to share with your teacher and classmates by clicking the response box below your response “Email me when my comment is published.”  

This is the last “What’s Going On In This Graph?” release of the school year.  We will return in early September.  Subscribe to the free NYT Learning Network newsletter to be notified of the next school year’s first release. 

Keep noticing and wondering.

raw_comment: The first thing I noticed in the graph was the size of each category and how there were four categories for both the infrastructure and family plan. Additionally, some of the categories include many smaller sub-divisions (such as the jobs and innovation category), though others don't include anything other than the plan itself (such as In-Home Care). What was even more suprising, in my opinion, was how close in size each section was, which shows that this plan is virtually divided equally. However, sub-divisions inside each category are not as equally distributed, such as in education. This category impacts me the most, as I am still a student going through the education system. Funding for schools, and other education related purposes, are so important to balance out because the education system has been lacking some attention these past fews year, particularly in Arizona. I find it very interesting that the ratio between the funding for teaching and the plan for preschools is about 1:22. That's quite surprising considering that teachers are needed for education to happen, and preschool does not need as much to function as an organization (not everyone goes to preschool even when it's free, less trips/extracurriculars than a primary/secondary school and generally less neccessary supplies). Lastly, I would like to mention that a potential title for this graph could be "U.S. Government Spending Plan." Very straight-forward and blunt, but it gets to the point.

2. **Layout techniques**:
- **Hierarchical nesting**: Large regions contain smaller subregions.
- **Partitioned by category**: The circle is split into two top-level groups.
- **Area encoding**: Region size represents amount.
- **Color grouping**: Two colors distinguish the two top-level plans.
- No axes, no faceting, no stacking.

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Plan (Infrastructure plan, Families plan) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue; top-level grouped region within the circle; legend |

| Program / line item within category (e.g., Roads and bridges, Affordable housing, Child care, Pell grants, etc.) | Categorical/nominal | Individual polygon region; text label |
| Amount ($ billions / trillions) | Quantitative | Area/size of regions; numeric text labels inside regions; totals in legend |

image_description:
1. **Chart type**: Circular hierarchical **treemap / Voronoi treemap**.

2. **Layout techniques**:
- **Hierarchical nesting**: Large regions contain smaller subregions.
- **Partitioned by category**: The circle is split into two top-level groups.
- **Area encoding**: Region size represents amount.
- **Color grouping**: Two colors distinguish the two top-level plans.
- No axes, no faceting, no stacking.

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Plan (Infrastructure plan, Families plan) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue; top-level grouped region within the circle; legend |
| Major spending category (e.g., Transportation, Buildings and Utilities, In-Home Care, Jobs and Innovation, Tax Credits, Child and Family Support, Education, I.R.S.) | Categorical/nominal | Nested region/grouping; text label |
| Program / line item within category (e.g., Roads and bridges, Affordable housing, Child care, Pell grants, etc.) | Categorical/nominal | Individual polygon region; text label |
| Amount ($ billions / trillions) | Quantitative | Area/size of regions; numeric text labels inside regions; totals in legend |

Visible note:
- Units are stated as **amounts on the chart in billions**, while top-level legend totals are shown in **trillions**.

image_description:
1. **Chart type**: Circular hierarchical **treemap / Voronoi treemap**.

2. **Layout techniques**:
- **Hierarchical nesting**: Large regions contain smaller subregions.
- **Partitioned by category**: The circle is split into two top-level groups.
- **Area encoding**: Region size represents amount.
- **Color grouping**: Two colors distinguish the two top-level plans.
- No axes, no faceting, no stacking.

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Plan (Infrastructure plan, Families plan) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue; top-level grouped region within the circle; legend |
| Major spending category (e.g., Transportation, Buildings and Utilities, In-Home Care, Jobs and Innovation, Tax Credits, Child and Family Support, Education, I.R.S.) | Categorical/nominal | Nested region/grouping; text label |
| Program / line item within category (e.g., Roads and bridges, Affordable housing, Child care, Pell grants, etc.) | Categorical/nominal | Individual polygon region; text label |
| Amount ($ billions / trillions) | Quantitative | Area/size of regions; numeric text labels inside regions; totals in legend |

Visible note:
- Units are stated as **amounts on the chart in billions**, while top-level legend totals are shown in **trillions**.

image_description:
1. **Chart type**: Circular hierarchical **treemap / Voronoi treemap**.

2. **Layout techniques**:
- **Hierarchical nesting**: Large regions contain smaller subregions.
- **Partitioned by category**: The circle is split into two top-level groups.
- **Area encoding**: Region size represents amount.
- **Color grouping**: Two colors distinguish the two top-level plans.
- No axes, no faceting, no stacking.

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Plan (Infrastructure plan, Families plan) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue; top-level grouped region within the circle; legend |
| Major spending category (e.g., Transportation, Buildings and Utilities, In-Home Care, Jobs and Innovation, Tax Credits, Child and Family Support, Education, I.R.S.) | Categorical/nominal | Nested region/grouping; text label |
| Program / line item within category (e.g., Roads and bridges, Affordable housing, Child care, Pell grants, etc.) | Categorical/nominal | Individual polygon region; text label |
| Amount ($ billions / trillions) | Quantitative | Area/size of regions; numeric text labels inside regions; totals in legend |

Visible note:
- Units are stated as **amounts on the chart in billions**, while top-level legend totals are shown in **trillions**.

image_description:
1. **Chart type**: Circular hierarchical **treemap / Voronoi treemap**.

2. **Layout techniques**:
- **Hierarchical nesting**: Large regions contain smaller subregions.
- **Partitioned by category**: The circle is split into two top-level groups.
- **Area encoding**: Region size represents amount.
- **Color grouping**: Two colors distinguish the two top-level plans.
- No axes, no faceting, no stacking.

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Plan (Infrastructure plan, Families plan) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue; top-level grouped region within the circle; legend |
| Major spending category (e.g., Transportation, Buildings and Utilities, In-Home Care, Jobs and Innovation, Tax Credits, Child and Family Support, Education, I.R.S.) | Categorical/nominal | Nested region/grouping; text label |
| Program / line item within category (e.g., Roads and bridges, Affordable housing, Child care, Pell grants, etc.) | Categorical/nominal | Individual polygon region; text label |
| Amount ($ billions / trillions) | Quantitative | Area/size of regions; numeric text labels inside regions; totals in legend |

Visible note:
- Units are stated as **amounts on the chart in billions**, while top-level legend totals are shown in **trillions**.
raw_comment:
The thing I notice right away is that the chart seems to be attempting to be a pie chart but falls a little short in the actual presentation of the chart. The fact that the chart is comprised of pieces instead of slices makes it feel a bit disorganized or misleading with its size. I notice that infrastructure is slightly bigger than the family section, meaning more money is being put into that. I also notice that infrastructure has more tiny pieces whereas the family section has larger pieces.
I wonder how each section was decided. I think putting together a budget, especially one of this size, is extremely difficult so I wonder how each amount of money was divided up so that the needs of each section would be met. I also wonder how different age groups will react to this budgeting. I know people that are younger, millennials and gen z, have been pushing for a lot of this green energy and free education stuff. It makes me think how older generations might feel, possibly seeing this as another way younger people have it easy. 
I think a lot of this will affect everyone in the US. As someone currently in community college I know this would benefit a lot of my friends and peers who struggle financially. I also know that affordable housing is extremely important as the cost of living is on the rise. Looking at my situation currently, I won't be able to leave home until my early 20s, something past generations didn't do.

Budgeting for Tomorrow: Biden's Plans for America Today

2. **Layout techniques**:
- **Hierarchical nesting**: Large regions contain smaller subregions.
- **Partitioned by category**: The circle is split into two top-level groups.
- **Area encoding**: Region size represents amount.
- **Color grouping**: Two colors distinguish the two top-level plans.
- No axes, no faceting, no stacking.

3. **Data variables**:

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Plan (Infrastructure plan, Families plan) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue; top-level grouped region within the circle; legend |
| Major spending category (e.g., Transportation, Buildings and Utilities, In-Home Care, Jobs and Innovation, Tax Credits, Child and Family Support, Education, I.R.S.) | Categorical/nominal | Nested region/grouping; text label |
| Program / line item within category (e.g., Roads and bridges, Affordable housing, Child care, Pell grants, etc.) | Categorical/nominal | Individual polygon region; text label |
| Amount ($ billions / trillions) | Quantitative | Area/size of regions; numeric text labels inside regions; totals in legend |
